title: FrameCast in the browser: choose the first screen
question: Same FrameCast look in all three. This picks how the first screen works. Keep the roll, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Finish the sentence
options.lineage: One plain sentence sets up the whole recording
options.thesis: You set up a recording by finishing one sentence, then press Record.
options.viewport: Record my [Whole screen] with [My mic] and [My face] for [Mike, JS Cleaning]; a big red Record under it, a small live preview, and your recordings down the right.
options.risk: The sentence has to stay short and literal for teammates whose first language is not English.

raised.raise: The recording timer uses fixed-width figures, so it never jumps as the seconds tick.
A recovered or new recording stays lit in the library until you open it.
A recording's length is drawn as length: longer videos get longer bars in the library and trimmer.
Colour always means a state: red recording, green saved, amber a browser limit.
One text size does most of the work; hierarchy comes from weight, not a ladder of sizes.

options.label: Pre-flight check
options.thesis: A big live preview with a green tick for every part, so you know it will work before you press Record.
materials: status rows with live mic meter
options.viewport: The live preview fills the left; on the right, Screen, Microphone with a moving level meter, Camera, Computer sound, Crash-proof saving and Space, each with its status, and Record at the bottom.
options.risk: Feels slower for quick problem reports; the checklist can read as more setup than it is.

options.label: Jobs first
options.lineage: The team's four real jobs as the starting point
options.thesis: Pick what you are recording (prospect, training, problem, handover) and the right settings are already on.
materials: four job tiles with colour edges
options.viewport: What are you recording? Four tiles across, each with its preset (camera, name card, chapters) and its own Record button; recent recordings in a row below.
options.risk: Changing a preset's setting takes one more step than the other two layouts.

options.label: Recording wall
options.lineage: A streaming service's rows of titles
options.thesis: A slim record bar on top and your recordings as rows by job, the one you land on growing to show its title and length.
options.viewport: Record bar with Screen, Mic and Face; then rows of Prospect videos, Training and Problem reports, the focused thumbnail larger with a purple edge.
options.case: Everyone knows how to browse it, and it is strongest for finding old videos; it loses on getting a new recording started.
options.risk: Puts the library first when the main job is recording something new.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Recordings listed like departures on a station board.
options.case: Nobody on the team thinks of their videos as departures; it would hide the Record button.
options.kept: Fixed-width figures for the recording timer.
options.risk: A costume of a station board on a working tool.

options.label: Boarding pass
options.thesis: Each recording as a ticket with segments.
options.viewport: A pass for the current recording beside a board of past ones.
options.case: Clear, but a ticket says travel, not video.
options.kept: New or recovered recordings stay lit until you open them.
options.risk: Novelty that wears off on day two.

options.label: Manual with tabs
options.thesis: Settings as tabbed pages of a software manual.
options.viewport: An open manual at the Record tab.
options.case: Its colours fight the FrameCast brand and it reads as documentation, not a recorder.
options.kept: One text size doing most of the work.

options.label: Transit map
options.thesis: Record, review and send drawn as stops on a line.
options.viewport: A line from Record to Sent with interchange circles.
options.case: Three steps do not need a map.

options.label: Dance score
options.thesis: A recording's timeline as a vertical score.
options.case: Too abstract for a quick video to a prospect.
options.risk: Nobody can read it without a lesson.
